notes: Bluetooth mode: with two or more boards linked, tap MAKE BT on one and it scans Bluetooth instead of Wi-Fi. The other boards keep Wi-Fi and share the channels.
Bluetooth devices are reported with their real addresses, so they count when you upload.
New terminal command: bt on / bt off.
Boot report: on every connect the board tells the app its firmware, slot, last reset reason and whether an update was rolled back.
If freshly updated firmware doesn't start within 30 seconds, the board restarts and goes back to the previous version on its own.
info also shows the boot report.
Terminal commands in Wardrive Go: help, info, status, ch, led, reboot. Unknown commands show the list.
led off keeps the status light dark, and the setting survives reboots.
Installs over Bluetooth on boards already running 1.2.
Firmware updates install over Bluetooth from Wardrive Go — one tap, no computer.
New flash layout: boards on 1.1.1 or older need one USB flash to reach 1.2. After that, updates come over Bluetooth.
If a new version fails to start, the board rolls back to the previous one.
The terminal's AP count shows the APs heard in each sweep.
ESP32-C5 scans 5 GHz (channels 36–48 and 149–161) as well as 2.4 GHz.
Several boards can link at once; the app splits the channels between them.
Each board has its own name (iosESP-XXXX).
First release: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi scanning streamed to Wardrive Go over Bluetooth.
